7: Division at the feast of Tabernacles

Jesus goes up to Jerusalem quietly and teaches in the Temple. The crowd argues about who he is. On the last day of the feast he cries out, "If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink." Guards sent to arrest him come back empty-handed.
The living water he promises is the Holy Spirit. Nobody can stay neutral about Jesus for long.
8: A woman caught in adultery is brought to Jesus. He says, "Let the one without sin throw the first stone," and tells her to go and sin no more. He declares, "I am the light of the world," and finally, "Before Abraham was, I am." They pick up stones to kill him.
Jesus neither condemns the sinner nor excuses the sin. "I am" is the name God gave to Moses, and his hearers understand the claim.
9: Jesus gives sight to a man blind from birth. The Pharisees question the man again and again and throw him out. Jesus finds him, and the man worships him.
The blind man ends up seeing more and more, while those sure of their own sight become blind. Suffering is not always a punishment for sin.
10: Jesus says he is the gate of the sheepfold and the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep. His sheep know his voice. At the feast of Dedication he says, "I and the Father are one," and they again try to stone him.
He gives his life freely; no one takes it from him. Being known by name by the Shepherd is the Christian's security.
11: Lazarus of Bethany dies, and Jesus arrives four days later. He tells Martha, "I am the resurrection and the life." He weeps at the tomb and then calls Lazarus out alive. The council decides that Jesus must die.
This is the greatest sign before the cross. Jesus weeps real tears, and he has power over death itself.
12: Mary of Bethany anoints Jesus' feet with costly perfume. He enters Jerusalem on a donkey. Some Greeks ask to see him, and he says that a grain of wheat must die to bear fruit, and that when he is lifted up he will draw all people to himself.
The cross is his glory, not his defeat. Life comes through self-giving.
13: At supper Jesus takes a towel and washes his disciples' feet. He foretells that Judas will betray him and Peter will deny him. He gives a new commandment: love one another as I have loved you.
The Lord does the work of a slave. Love like his is the mark by which his disciples are to be known.
14: The way, the truth and the life

Jesus tells the disciples not to be troubled: he goes to prepare a place for them. He says, "I am the way, the truth and the life," and "Whoever has seen me has seen the Father." He promises to send the Holy Spirit.
Jesus is not only a guide to God; he is the way. To know him is to know the Father.
15: Jesus says he is the true vine and his disciples are the branches. Cut off from him they can do nothing; remaining in him they bear much fruit. He calls them friends, and warns that the world will hate them as it hated him.
The Christian life is staying joined to Christ. "Greater love has no one than this, to lay down his life for his friends."
16: Jesus says it is good for the disciples that he goes, because then the Spirit will come and lead them into all truth. They will weep, but their grief will become joy, like a mother's after birth.
"In the world you will have trouble; but take courage, I have overcome the world."
17: Jesus lifts his eyes to heaven and prays to the Father: for himself, for the apostles, and for all who will believe through their word. He asks that they may all be one.
This is the prayer of our High Priest on the night before he died. The unity of Christians was among his last requests.
18: Jesus is arrested in a garden and steps forward himself. Peter denies him three times in the courtyard. Before Pilate Jesus says, "My kingdom is not of this world," and that he came to bear witness to the truth. Pilate asks, "What is truth?"
In John, Jesus is in command even as a prisoner. Truth himself stands in front of a judge who will not look for it.
19: Jesus is scourged, crowned with thorns and crucified. From the cross he gives his mother to the beloved disciple. He says, "It is finished," and dies. A soldier pierces his side, and blood and water flow out. He is buried in a new tomb.
"Behold your mother" gives Mary to every disciple. The Fathers saw the blood and water as signs of the Eucharist and baptism.
20: Mary Magdalene finds the tomb empty, and the risen Jesus calls her by name. That evening he breathes on the apostles and gives them power to forgive sins. Thomas doubts until he sees the wounds, then says, "My Lord and my God."
Here the sacrament of confession is given. "Blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe" is said about us.
21: The risen Jesus appears on the shore of Galilee and gives the disciples a huge catch of fish. Three times he asks Peter, "Do you love me?" and three times tells him to feed his sheep.
Peter's three denials are healed by three declarations of love. Jesus entrusts his whole flock to him.
